cues.en: If I'm sitting next to a swimming pool, somebody dives in, and she's not too pretty, so I can think of something else. I think of the waves and things that have formed in the water, and when lots of people have dived in the pool, there's a very great choppiness of all these waves all over the water, and to think that it's possible, maybe, that in those waves is a clue as to what's happening in the pool, that some sort of insect or something with sufficient cleverness could...
cues.zh: 假设我坐在游泳池边，有人跳进水里，她长得不太好看，所以我可以想点别的。我想到水波以及水中形成的各种形状，当很多人跳进泳池时，整个水面上会泛起非常剧烈的波纹。然后想，也许有可能，这些波纹里藏着泳池中正在发生什么的线索，某种昆虫或其他足够聪明的东西可以……

cues.en: sit in the corner of the pool and just be disturbed by the waves. And by the nature of the irregularities and bumping of the waves, have figured out who jumped in, where and when, and what's happening all over the pool. And that's what we're doing when we're looking at something. The light that comes out of it is waves, just like in the swimming pool, except in three dimensions, instead of the two dimensions of the pool, as they're going in all directions. And we have an eighth of an inch black hole into which these things go.
cues.zh: 坐在泳池角落，仅仅通过感受水波的扰动。通过水波的不规则性和碰撞特性，就能推断出是谁跳了进来、在何时何地跳的，以及整个泳池里正在发生什么。这就是我们观察事物时所做的。从物体发出的光是波，就像游泳池里的波一样，只不过是在三维空间中，而不是泳池的二维空间，因为光向四面八方传播。我们有一个八分之一英寸的“黑洞”，这些东西会进入其中。

cues.en: which is particularly sensitive to the parts of the waves that are coming in a particular direction. It's not particularly sensitive when they're coming in at the wrong angle, which we say is from the corner of our eye. And if we want to get more information in the corner of our eye, we scribble this ball about so that the hole moves from place to place. Then, it's quite wonderful that we can figure out so easy. That's really because the right waves are easier than the...
cues.zh: 它对来自特定方向的那部分波特别敏感。当波以错误的角度射入时，它就不那么敏感了，我们称之为余光。如果我们想用余光获取更多信息，就快速移动这个球，让那个“洞”从一个位置移到另一个位置。然后，非常奇妙的是，我们能如此轻易地弄清楚。这其实是因为正确的波比……更容易。

cues.en: The waves in the water are a little bit more complicated. It would have been harder for the bug than for us, but it's the same idea, to figure out what the thing is that we're looking at, at a distance. And this is kind of incredible, because when I'm looking at you, someone standing to my left can see somebody who's standing at my right. That is, the light could be going right across this way, the waves are going this way, the waves are going this way, the waves are going this way. It's just a complete network. Now, it's easy to think of them as arrows passing each other.
cues.zh: 水里的波纹要稍微复杂一些。虫子要弄明白会比我们更费劲，但原理是一样的，都是从远处搞清楚我们看到的是什么。这其实很不可思议，因为当我在看着你时，站在我左边的人可以看到站在我右边的人。也就是说，光线可以这样横穿过去，波往这个方向走，往那个方向走，往各个方向走。这就是一个交织的网络。我们很容易把它们想象成互相交错而过的箭头。

cues.en: But that's not the way it is, because all it is is something shaking. It's called the electric field, but we don't have to bother with what it is. It's just like the water height is going up and down. So there's some quantities shaking about here. And in a combination of motions that's so elaborate and complicated that that result is to produce an influence which makes me see you at the same time completely undisturbed by the fact that there are influences that represent the other guy seeing him on this side. So that there's this tremendous mess.
cues.zh: 但事实并非如此，因为归根结底只是某种东西在振动。它被称为电场，不过我们不用去纠结它究竟是什么。它就像水面的高度在上下起伏一样。所以这里是有某些量在振动。这些运动的组合极其精细复杂，其结果产生了一种效应，让我能看到你，与此同时，又完全不受另一边有人看着别人的光线所干扰。于是，空间中就形成了一团极其复杂的混乱——

cues.en: of waves all over in space, which we call, which is the light bouncing around the room and going from one thing to the other. Because, of course, most of the room doesn't have eighth-inch black holes. It's not interested in that light, but the light's there anyway. I mean, it bounces off this, and it bounces off that, that all this is going on, and yet we can sort it out with this instrument.
cues.zh: 充斥在整个空间的波，也就是在房间里四处弹跳、在物体间来回穿梭的光。因为房间的大多数地方当然没有八分之一英寸的黑洞（指瞳孔）。它们对光毫无兴趣，但光依然在那里。我的意思是，光从这里反射，又从那里反射，这一切都在不断发生，而我们却能借助眼睛这件仪器把它们梳理得清清楚楚。

cues.en: But beside all that, you see, those waves that I was talking about in the water, maybe they're so big, some of them, and then you could have slower swashes, which are longer and shorter. Perhaps our animal who's making his study is only using waves between this length and that length. So it turns out that the eye is only using waves between this length and that length, except those two lengths are a hundred thousandths of an inch. A hundred thousandth of an inch, Pete.
cues.zh: 但除此之外，你看，我刚才说的水里那些波，也许有些波非常大，然后还会有更慢的波涌，有长有短。也许我们这只做研究的动物，只利用这个长度和那个长度之间的波。所以结果就是，眼睛只利用这个长度和那个长度之间的波，只不过这两个长度之间只差十万分之一英寸。十万分之一英寸啊，Pete。

cues.en: And what about the slower swashes, the waves that go more slowly, that have a longer distance from crest to trunk? Those represent heat. We feel those, but our eye doesn't see them focused very well. We don't, in fact, at all. The shorter waves are blue, the longer waves are red, but when it gets longer than that, we call it infrared. All this is in there at the same time. That's the heat. Pit vipers that got down here in the desert, they have a little
cues.zh: 那更慢的波涌呢？那些传播得更慢、波峰到波谷距离更长的波呢？它们代表热。我们能感觉到它们，但眼睛没法很好地把它们聚焦起来。事实上，我们根本看不到。较短的波是蓝色，较长的波是红色，但如果再长下去，我们就叫它红外线。所有这些同时都在那里。那就是热。来到这沙漠里的蝮蛇，它们有个小

cues.en: thing that they can see the longer waves and pick out mice, which are radiating their heat, their longer waves, by their body heat, by looking at them with this eye, which is the pit of the pit viper. But we can't, we don't, are able to do that. And then these waves get longer and longer, and you know, all through the same space, all these things are going on at the same time. So that in this space, there's not only my vision of you,
cues.zh: 东西，能让它们看见更长的波，并挑出老鼠——老鼠因体温而辐射热量，也就是更长的波；蝮蛇就是用这只眼睛看它们，这只眼睛就是蝮蛇的颊窝。但我们不能，我们做不到。然后这些波越来越长，你知道，全都穿过同一个空间，所有这一切同时发生。所以在这个空间里，不只有我看到的你，

cues.en: but information from Moscow radio that's being broadcast at the present moment and the seeing of somebody from Peru. All the radio waves are just the same kind of waves, only longer waves. And there's the radar from the airplane, which is looking at the ground to figure out where it is, which is coming through this room at the same time. Plus the x-ray, cosmic rays, and all these other things, which are the same kind of waves, exactly the same waves, but shorter, faster, or longer, slower. It's exactly the same thing. So this...
cues.zh: 还有此刻正在广播的莫斯科电台的信息，以及秘鲁某人的所见。所有无线电波都是同一种波，只是波长更长。还有飞机上的雷达，它正向下扫描地面以确定自己的位置，同时也在穿过这个房间。再加上X射线、宇宙射线，以及所有这些东西，它们都是同一种波，完全相同的波，只是更短、更快，或更长、更慢。完全是一回事。所以这个……

cues.en: big field, this area of irregular motions of this electric field, this vibration, contains this tremendous information, and it's all really there. That's what gets you. If you don't believe it, then you pick a piece of wire and connect it to a box.
cues.zh: 广阔的场，电场这些不规则的运动、这些振动，蕴含着巨大的信息，而这一切都真实存在。这才是最震撼的地方。你要是不信，就拿根导线接到一个盒子上。

cues.en: And in the wire, the electrons will be pushed back and forth by this electric field, swashing just at the right speed for a certain kind of long ways. And you turn some knobs on the box to get the swashing just right, and you hear Radio Moscow. Now, you know that it was there. How else did it get there? It was there all the time. It was only when you turn on the radio that you notice it. But that all these things are going through the room at the same time, which everybody knows. But you've got to stop and think about it to really get the pleasure.
cues.zh: 在导线里，电场会让电子来回运动，以恰当的速度为某种长波而振荡。你转动盒子上的几个旋钮，把这种振荡调准，就听到了 Radio Moscow。现在你知道它一直都在。不然它怎么会到那儿？它一直都在那儿。只有你打开收音机，才会注意到它。所有这些信号同时穿过房间，这谁都知道。但你得停下来想一想，才能真正体会到其中的乐趣。

cues.en: About the complexity the inconceivable Nature of nature in January 1986 the space shuttle Challenger exploded
cues.zh: 关于复杂性，关于自然那不可思议的本质。1986年1月，挑战者号航天飞机爆炸了。
